sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The explanation is that the distinction between son and servant applies to the soul as it comes in a chain of descent, but in its root in Atzmus itself, both aspects are one, and this applies to Torah and mitzvos as well, requiring the nullification of a servant in Torah study.

translations.translation: And the point of the explanation in this,
that this that a son and a servant are two matters,
is in the soul as it comes in a chain of descent,
but in the root of the soul as it is rooted in the Awtsmoos itself,
the two matters within it are one.
And likewise is it in Torah and mitzvos,
that as they are in the Awtsmoos,
both of them are one matter.
And therefore,
also in the study of Torah there must be also the nullification of a servant.
For through the study of Torah in the aspect of a son alone,
the connection of Yisrael to the Torah
is in the level of Torah as it comes in a chain of descent
[that Torah and mitzvos become two matters],
and in order that the connection be in the essence of Torah as it is rooted in the Awtsmoos
[where Torah and mitzvos are one],
it is through that in his Torah study both matters are emphasized.
For Torah is not in heaven, but rather it is given into his jurisdiction,
therefore his rulings are specifically according to his understanding and we do not pay attention to a Heavenly Voice
— the reality of a son,
and together with this he accepts upon himself the yoke of Torah,
that the Torah is his "master" and he is nullified to the Torah like a servant upon whom the yoke of the master is placed.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The essence of wisdom is that repentance and good deeds accompany it, for in Torah study there must be the nullification of repentance and the nullification of good deeds, thereby grasping the root of Torah in the Awtsmoos.

translations.translation: And this is "the essence of wisdom is repentance and good deeds,"
that the essence of Torah is that repentance and good deeds be with it.
For in addition to that Torah brings to repentance and good deeds,
repentance and good deeds must be with it,
with the Torah itself,
that in the study of Torah there should also be the nullification of repentance and good deeds.
[And it may be said,
that this that it says that repentance and good deeds be with it,
it is,
because the nullification of repentance
(that a person goes out of his existence,
bound from here),
is from his feeling,
and therefore even in the nullification there is mixed
(in subtlety)
his existence,
and the true nullification is the nullification of good deeds,
for this that the fulfillment of mitzvos is in the manner of acceptance of the yoke is not from his will but from the yoke of the kingdom of heaven placed upon him
(as above end of section 4).
And especially according to the explanation above
(section 6)
that the intention in "good deeds" is to the mitzvos
(deeds)
themselves,
for according to this explanation,
the nullification of good deeds is that there is not felt in it even this that he is nullified to the Master,
and what is felt is only the Supernal Will.
And "the essence of wisdom is that repentance and good deeds be with it,"
that in his Torah study there should be the nullification of repentance and also the nullification of good deeds].
And this matter is the essence of Torah,
for through this one grasps the core and root of Torah as it is rooted in the Awtsmoos.

sections.sectionSummaryBrief: The reason this saying was specifically Rava's constant adage is because his style of study emphasized the existence of the student, requiring the nullification of repentance and good deeds.

translations.translation: And it may be added,
that the reason for this that this statement
("the essence of wisdom is repentance and good deeds")
was the constant adage of Rava specifically,
is because in Torah study there are two general modes,
the mode of study of Abaye and the mode of study of Rava
[therefore,
in the disputes of Abaye and Rava are included all the matters of the Oral Torah].
And the difference between the two modes is as stated in the Gemara,
"In the house of Abaye they would gnaw bones; in the house of Rava they would eat fatty meat."
And since the Torah study of Rava was in the manner of "fatty meat"
(clear, expansive laws),
that in study in this manner the existence of the studying person is emphasized,
and especially that his conduct was that before he opened for the sages he would say a humorous word,
therefore the statement "the essence of wisdom is repentance and good deeds" was his constant adage,
that in Torah study there must also be the nullification of repentance and of good deeds.
